newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ministers in emergency talks after blast.
newsitem.headline: French ministers in emergency talks after blast.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe met his interior and justice ministers for emergency talks on Monday after a bomb suspected to have been planted by Corsican separatists exploded at his mayoral office in Bordeaux.
The powerful blast caused widespread damage in the southwestern city's elegant 18th century city hall which Juppe had left several hours before the attack, on Saturday.
Investigators have said Corsican guerrillas, who recently threatened to take their bombing campaign to mainland France, could be responsible for the attack.
Juppe met Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and Justice Minister Jacques Toubon at his Matignon office.

Juppe has ordered a crackdown on Corsican separatists who are blamed for dozens of bomb attack on the French Mediterranean island since the summer, despite a truce. Nationalist leaders have accused him of blocking secret talks aimed at resolving their differences.
While declining to blame Corsican guerrillas for the attack, Juppe said in an television interview on Sunday night he would stick to his policy of firmness towards the separatists.
"This policy is difficult to carry out because we are facing terrorists...The state cannot yield and must not be intimidated. We will remain fully determined regarding Corsica," he said.

The clandestine Corsican National Liberation Front - Historical Wing (FLNC) last week claimed responsibility for a bomb attack outside the law courts in Aix-en-Provence in southern France, its first on the mainland in several years.
The guerrillas have waged a campaign of bombing on the holiday island for two decades in search of greater autonomy from Paris.
